content: Dr. Bernard J. Cigrand, a dentist by profession, is widely recognized as the Father of Flag Day in the United States. Born in 1866 and passing in 1932, he practiced dentistry in Chicago and served as the third dean of the University of Illinois at Chicago College of Dentistry from 1903 to 1906. In 1885, while working as a grade school teacher in Waubeka, Wisconsin, Dr. Cigrand organized the first formal and recognized observance of Flag Day at Stony Hill School. This school has since been restored, and a bust of Dr. Cigrand is displayed at the National Flag Day Americanism Center in Waubeka to honor his contributions. From the late 1880s onward, Dr. Cigrand traveled extensively across the country, delivering speeches that emphasized patriotism, respect for the American flag, and the importance of establishing an annual Flag Day on June 14. This date commemorates the adoption of the Stars and Stripes by the Continental Congress in 1777. He became president of the American Flag Day Association and later the National Flag Day Society, which provided him with organizational support to further his cause. Dr. Cigrand once noted that he had delivered 2,188 speeches on patriotism and the flag. In 1899, Dr. Cigrand joined the teaching staff at the UIC College of Dentistry. In 1900, he was elected by his colleagues to represent the faculty at the Paris International Congress of Educators. He also served as secretary of the faculty before being appointed dean. After his tenure as dean, he continued teaching at the college well into the 1920s and contributed articles to five Chicago newspapers. Dr. Cigrand’s tireless advocacy for Flag Day spanned over three decades. In 1916, President Woodrow Wilson officially proclaimed June 14 as Flag Day, a milestone that was later solidified into law by the United States Congress in 1949. The public widely credited Dr. Cigrand for his pivotal role in establishing the holiday, with the Chicago Tribune remarking that he almost singlehandedly brought Flag Day into existence.
